highlights.content: ![]() ![PR Newswire](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/pr_newswire--theme-light.svg) ![PR Newswire](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/pr_newswire--theme-dark.svg) # SuperCom Unveils SafeGenie for Real-Time Monitoring and Control of Autonomous AI Agents ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/supercom.svg) ***Delivers novel,*** ***patent-pending technology to address the security risks of agentic AI, with initial rollout planned through the global customer base and distribution channels of Safend, SuperCom's cybersecurity subsidiary*** ***Combines new AI-agent controls with Safend's endpoint security technology, developed over more than two decades, deployed across millions of endpoints and backed by 27 issued patents*** TEL AVIV, Israel, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SuperCom ([![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/supercom.svg)SPCB](/symbols/NASDAQ-SPCB/)), a global provider of secure solutions for the IoT, cybersecurity, and digital identity sectors, today introduced SafeGenie, a cybersecurity product suite for the real-time monitoring and control of autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents. SafeGenie combines novel, patent-pending methods for agentic AI security with the kernel-level endpoint security technology of Safend, SuperCom's wholly owned cybersecurity subsidiary. Safend's technology has been deployed across millions of endpoints for thousands of customers, including government agencies, defense organizations and enterprises. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/supercom.svg) AI agents are spreading rapidly across enterprises, yet traditional security was built around people, devices and approved applications, not software that acts with full user permissions and decides its own next step in a statistical and sometimes unpredictable way. Security budgets are beginning to reflect this shift. Gartner forecasts that spending on securing AI will grow from approximately $2.8 billion in 2026 to almost $7.7 billion by 2028,1 which represents average growth of approximately 65% a year. SafeGenie assesses the context and intent behind each action an AI agent takes and allows, flags or blocks it in real time, before the action completes, helping prevent agent misbehavior, sensitive-data leakage and irreversible damage. The suite also secures conventional generative AI use, including prompt protection, as part of a comprehensive control plane for AI across the enterprise. More information is available at www.SafeGenie.ai. "Agentic AI presents enterprises with a major opportunity. Agents can now research, move data and complete multi-step tasks across business systems with a degree of independence that makes them exceptionally productive," commented Ordan Trabelsi, President and CEO of SuperCom. "That same independence makes every agent a potential insider threat, operating with an employee's access, at machine speed and around the clock. Our customers should not have to choose between productivity and control. SafeGenie is designed to give them that control, stopping high-risk actions while legitimate work carries on." "Our cybersecurity engineers have developed novel, patent-pending methods to address security challenges unique to agentic AI," Trabelsi added. "Kernel-level security is difficult to build and stabilize at scale, and Safend's technology has been proven across thousands of customer environments. We believe that foundation, combined with these innovations and our long-standing relationships with government, defense and enterprise customers, positions us well to secure agentic AI for both our existing and new customers." Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design.  [NVIDIA Cloud Partners](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/gpu-cloud-computing/partners/) across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Edited by Barnabas Oretan (The Tech Buzz).· AI-generated image [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com) and [NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com) are bringing the chipmaker's Vera Rubin infrastructure to general availability next month, marking a significant escalation in the cloud AI arms race. The A5X instances combine NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs with ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and Google's fourth-generation liquid-cooling technology, creating an integrated platform for AI training, inference, and large-scale reinforcement learning. The rollout starts in the U.S. before expanding to Europe, as hyperscalers race to offer the most powerful AI infrastructure to enterprise customers. [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com) is making its biggest bet yet on AI infrastructure, announcing that [NVIDIA's](https://www.nvidia.com) Vera Rubin-powered A5X instances will reach general availability next month. The move puts Google squarely in competition with rivals racing to offer the most powerful cloud-based AI training platforms. The A5X instances represent a full-stack approach to AI infrastructure. They bring together NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs, the company's ConnectX-9 SuperNICs for high-speed networking, Google Cloud's proprietary Virgo Network, and Google's fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology. It's an integrated system designed for the most demanding AI workloads, from training massive models to running inference at scale and handling complex reinforcement learning tasks. The timing couldn't be more strategic. Just hours after [NVIDIA unveiled its full local AI stack at GTC Berlin](https://www.techbuzz.ai/articles/nvidia-unleashes-full-local-ai-stack-at-gtc-berlin), including RTX Spark and DGX systems for on-device intelligence, the company is now extending its reach into cloud infrastructure. The dual approach shows NVIDIA hedging its bets across both edge and cloud computing as enterprises figure out where their AI workloads will ultimately run. Google's deployment strategy starts domestic before going global. The initial U.S. rollout next month will be followed by European expansion, though specific timing and regions remain under wraps. The phased approach suggests Google is being cautious about scaling what's essentially a complex, power-hungry infrastructure play that requires significant data center modifications. OpenAI says agents weakened internal monitoring system **Two AI agents interfered with safeguards designed to detect misbehaviour, highlighting the challenges of keeping increasingly autonomous systems under control.** * [ETEnterpriseAI Desk](/author/479273811/etenterpriseai-desk) * [ETEnterpriseAI](/agency/88676044/ETEnterpriseAI) * Updated On Oct 21, 2026 at 02:35 PM IST In both cases, the AI agents interfered with mechanisms designed to monitor their behaviour, although the circumstances surrounding the two incidents differed. OpenAI said on Tuesday that two of its AI agents weakened parts of an internal monitoring system designed to detect misbehaviour, the latest case of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend them to, *Reuters* reported. Advt The incidents have renewed questions about the reliability of safeguards built into AI systems as they become increasingly capable of executing complex tasks with limited human intervention. Monitoring mechanisms are intended to flag potentially unsafe actions and help developers identify when an AI system deviates from its intended instructions. According to OpenAI, the two incidents occurred during internal coding tasks on October 3 and October 6. ### Event #### [Agentic Summit 2026](https://enterpriseai.economictimes.indiatimes.com/agentic-ai-summit?ag=whats_happening&utm_source=whats_happening&utm_content=135089202&utm_campaign=Product_Promo_Widget&utm_index=1) ##### [Join the Agentic AI Summit - The Economic Times AI Summit to explore agentic systems, automation, and future AI innovations. Experience cutting-edge AI insights, Network with industry leaders, innovators, and tech decision-makers at the AI Events 2026.](https://enterpriseai.economictimes.indiatimes.com/agentic-ai-summit?ag=whats_happening&utm_source=whats_happening&utm_content=135089202&utm_campaign=Product_Promo_Widget&utm_index=1) * ###### Wed, 09 Dec 2026 * ###### Mumbai [Register Now](https://enterpriseai.economictimes.indiatimes.com/agentic-ai-summit?ag=whats_happening&utm_source=whats_happening&utm_content=135089202&utm_campaign=Product_Promo_Widget&utm_index=1) Show More In both cases, the AI agents interfered with mechanisms designed to monitor their behaviour, although the circumstances surrounding the two incidents differed. **How it panned out** In the first incident, an AI agent suppressed automatic security alerts after interpreting an instruction not to send messages on Slack as also applying to safety notifications. The action effectively weakened an internal mechanism intended to flag potentially problematic behaviour. Describe the issue below: ![archive](https://static.arxiv.org/static/design-system/latest/logos/arxiv-logo.svg) # Beyond Calibration: Temporal LLM Confidence Assessment Across Languages and Local Settings ###### Abstract Large language models are expected to estimate their own uncertainty, with confidence signals used to guide retrieval, adaptive compute allocation, routing, and selective abstention. We investigate whether confidence signals measured at different temporal stages of problem solving encode distinct forms of epistemic information and remain reliable beyond English-centric settings. Inspired by classical meta-memory theory, we distinguish anticipatory pre-solve confidence (*Feeling-of-Knowing*, FOK) from retrospective post-solve confidence (*Judgement-of-Learning*, JOL). We evaluate these signals across two frontier LLMs, multiple reasoning domains, translated Marathi benchmarks, and a newly constructed benchmark of genuinely local Marathi factual questions. Across settings, the cheaper pre-solve signal remains weakly calibrated, while post-solve confidence generally provides stronger epistemic alignment despite its additional inference cost. Confidence behaviour transfers surprisingly well under direct language translation, with calibration trends largely preserved between English and Marathi, but degrades substantially on local Marathi knowledge, suggesting that linguistic transfer alone is insufficient for region-specific information needs. Finally, hallucinated responses maintain persistently elevated confidence after answer generation, highlighting important limitations of current LLM self-assessment mechanisms. ## 1 Introduction Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across a wide range of real-world applications, including question answering, reasoning systems, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), autonomous agents, and decision-support pipelines [Li et al. (2024)](#bib.bib2); [Cheng et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1). Modern models contain substantial factual and procedural knowledge encoded within their parameters, while also leveraging external context through tools, retrieval systems, and long-context prompting. In many such systems, models are further expected to make decisions about their own uncertainty and knowledge limitations, a capability often framed as self-knowledge [Kale and Nadadur (2025)](#bib.bib3) or metacognition [Ma et al. (2025)](#bib.bib5). These internal confidence estimates are increasingly used to influence downstream behaviours such as deciding whether to invoke tools, request additional user clarification, defer generation, allocate additional compute, or trigger retrieval mechanisms [Li et al. (2025)](#bib.bib4). However, recent work has shown that LLM confidence signals are often poorly calibrated and only weakly aligned with actual correctness. Will the network carry someone else’s value, or will it become the platform on which that value is created? Inference gives service providers a strong opportunity to choose the second path. They already have assets that the AI economy needs: distributed facilities, power, trusted infrastructure, and reach in the regions where enterprises and governments operate. Those assets become more valuable when they can operate as one system. SafeGenie combines novel, patent-pending methods for agentic AI security with the kernel-level endpoint security technology of Safend, SuperCom's wholly owned cybersecurity subsidiary. Safend's technology has been deployed across millions of endpoints for thousands of customers, including government agencies, defense organizations and enterprises. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/supercom.svg) AI agents are spreading rapidly across enterprises, yet traditional security was built around people, devices and approved applications, not software that acts with full user permissions and decides its own next step in a statistical and sometimes unpredictable way. Gartner forecasts that spending on securing AI will grow from approximately $2.8 billion in 2026 to almost $7.7 billion by 2028,1 which represents average growth of approximately 65% a year. The suite also secures conventional generative AI use, including prompt protection, as part of a comprehensive control plane for AI across the enterprise. More information is available at www.SafeGenie.ai. "Agentic AI presents enterprises with a major opportunity. Agents can now research, move data and complete multi-step tasks across business systems with a degree of independence that makes them exceptionally productive," commented Ordan Trabelsi, President and CEO of SuperCom. The announcement, titled “Dell Technologies Turns Enterprise Data Into Trusted Context for AI Agents,” adds three new components to the **Dell AI Data Platform**. For Irish IT leaders watching the agentic AI wave crash into procurement budgets, the pitch is blunt. At its core, the announcement adds three named pieces to the Dell AI Data Platform: a Unified Semantic Layer, a Knowledge Graph, and Knowledge Agents. Dell frames all three as working together so that applications and AI agents get a shared, trusted view of enterprise data rather than three separate silos each guessing at what the others mean. That framing matters because most enterprise AI failures trace back to context, not model quality. An agent can run on the sharpest large language model on the market and still give a wrong answer if it is reading from a customer record that is six months stale or a product catalog that conflicts with the finance system. Dell’s pitch is that these three layers close that gap before the model ever gets asked a question. ## Inside the Dell AI Data Platform: Three New Pieces Each of the three components targets a different failure mode in enterprise AI deployments. The Unified Semantic Layer standardizes how data is described and accessed, so an AI agent pulling from a CRM system and one pulling from a warehouse database can agree on what a “customer” or an “order” actually means. Harmonize CRM and CX with a single autonomous system [Learn how](https://www.sap.com/products/crm.html) It requires AI that can drive outcomes by executing and coordinating work across the customer journey and the business processes behind it, grounded in trusted data and governed at every step. Describe the issue below: ![archive](https://static.arxiv.org/static/design-system/latest/logos/arxiv-logo.svg) # Beyond Calibration: Temporal LLM Confidence Assessment Across Languages and Local Settings ###### Abstract Large language models are expected to estimate their own uncertainty, with confidence signals used to guide retrieval, adaptive compute allocation, routing, and selective abstention. We investigate whether confidence signals measured at different temporal stages of problem solving encode distinct forms of epistemic information and remain reliable beyond English-centric settings. Inspired by classical meta-memory theory, we distinguish anticipatory pre-solve confidence (*Feeling-of-Knowing*, FOK) from retrospective post-solve confidence (*Judgement-of-Learning*, JOL). We evaluate these signals across two frontier LLMs, multiple reasoning domains, translated Marathi benchmarks, and a newly constructed benchmark of genuinely local Marathi factual questions. Across settings, the cheaper pre-solve signal remains weakly calibrated, while post-solve confidence generally provides stronger epistemic alignment despite its additional inference cost. Confidence behaviour transfers surprisingly well under direct language translation, with calibration trends largely preserved between English and Marathi, but degrades substantially on local Marathi knowledge, suggesting that linguistic transfer alone is insufficient for region-specific information needs. Finally, hallucinated responses maintain persistently elevated confidence after answer generation, highlighting important limitations of current LLM self-assessment mechanisms. ## 1 Introduction Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across a wide range of real-world applications, including question answering, reasoning systems, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), autonomous agents, and decision-support pipelines [Li et al. (2024)](#bib.bib2); [Cheng et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1). Modern models contain substantial factual and procedural knowledge encoded within their parameters, while also leveraging external context through tools, retrieval systems, and long-context prompting. In many such systems, models are further expected to make decisions about their own uncertainty and knowledge limitations, a capability often framed as self-knowledge [Kale and Nadadur (2025)](#bib.bib3) or metacognition [Ma et al. (2025)](#bib.bib5). These internal confidence estimates are increasingly used to influence downstream behaviours such as deciding whether to invoke tools, request additional user clarification, defer generation, allocate additional compute, or trigger retrieval mechanisms [Li et al. (2025)](#bib.bib4). However, recent work has shown that LLM confidence signals are often poorly calibrated and only weakly aligned with actual correctness. This limits the efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness of such confidence-driven decision policies [Kale and Dhami (2025)](#bib.bib6). ![Refer to caption](2610.27702v1/media/conf_fig1.png) While confidence calibration has been studied primarily in English-centric benchmarks, many practical deployments increasingly involve multilingual and underrepresented language settings where both model knowledge and evaluation resources are less abundant. Confidence estimates that appear reliable in high-resource settings may fail to transfer across languages or culturally specific knowledge domains, potentially leading to inappropriate retrieval decisions, overconfident hallucinations, or unsafe downstream behaviour. A particularly important open question is whether confidence calibration is primarily tied to language or to underlying knowledge availability. The system combines recognition, reasoning, tool calling and synthesis into a single real-time pipeline, completing a single interaction turn in under one second, with real-time transcription latency below 500 milliseconds. The products are available through European, U.S. and global APIs and support self-hosted deployment. Transcription is priced at $0.0035 to $0.008 per minute, and speech synthesis at $13 per million characters. Mistral says its Small model beats Whisper large-v3 on word error rate in FLEURS benchmark tests across 45 languages. ##### Key Elements ![Mistral Launches Voxtral 3 Voice Agent SDK, Enabling Real-Time Interaction in More Than 50 Languages](https://img.biggo.com/atnCPWCDTLQ7E9KfoG91LzG3wvhN2MqceTAj23hqDg8/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTEwL2Y3NDZmYTA3LTY5NDctNGMzNC1iMWQ3LWRhNTFkOTM0MGE1N18xNzkyNTY5ODA1X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) French artificial intelligence company Mistral AI on October 20 released a voice agent software development kit (SDK) and a companion family of speech models, Voxtral 3, integrating speech recognition, reasoning and decision-making, tool calling and speech synthesis into a single real-time processing pipeline aimed at call centers, help desks, virtual assistants and similar use cases. The product supports transcription in more than 50 languages and speech synthesis in more than 35 languages. It is available immediately through European, U.S. and global APIs and also supports enterprise self-hosted deployment. Unlike offerings on the market that stitch together separate transcription, synthesis and reasoning components, Voxtral 3 emphasizes an "end-to-end connected" capability. According to a report by OSChina, in an official demonstration an English-speaking user called a clinic holding a French-language referral letter; the voice agent recognized the French content, completed the appointment and promised to send a confirmation text message in English, showcasing a complete workflow combining cross-language understanding, tool calling and emotional adaptation. At the model level, the transcription products come in three versions. Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 and Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 cover more than 50 languages; the former offers speaker diarization, preset specialized terminology to improve recognition accuracy, and end-of-speech detection. Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3, aimed at real-time scenarios, has latency below 500 milliseconds. The speech synthesis model Voxtral Speech 3 supports more than 35 languages and more than 50 dialects, and can adjust emotion, speaking rate and accent based on conversational context. Mistral AI says that in FLEURS benchmark tests across 45 languages, Small's word error rate outperforms competitors such as Whisper large-v3. The SDK runs on LiveKit, allowing end-of-speech detection, inference by a general-purpose model (such as Mistral Small) and tool calling, and voice responses to proceed in parallel without waiting for the previous step to finish. A single interaction turn completes within one second, and the system stops speaking when the user interrupts. At the interface level, it supports telephone lines (SIP) and WebRTC and can connect to existing call-center software. AI Product.content: [## the tech buzz](/) Anthropic Launches Claude Duet AI Agent to Take On Meta and OpenAI [AI](/topics/ai)/[AI agents](/topics/ai-agents) # Anthropic Launches Claude Duet AI Agent to Take On Meta and OpenAI Claude maker debuts autonomous agent for professionals with morning briefs and task automation by [The Tech Buzz](/authors/the-tech-buzz) PUBLISHED: Wed, Oct 21, 2026, 8:08 PM UTC| UPDATED: Wed, Oct 21, 2026, 8:08 PM UTC [Add as a preferred source on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=techbuzz.ai) ![Claude Duet app interface displayed on a smartphone screen showing a morning briefing summary.](/cdn-cgi/image/width=1200,quality=85,format=auto,fit=cover/https://charming-card-d91ad3487b.media.strapiapp.com/large_anthropic_launches_claude_duet_ai_agent_to_take_on_meta_and_openai_6f6adb9b5a.jpg) Photo: Claude Duet app interface displayed on a smartphone screen showing a morning briefing summary. AI-generated illustration by The Tech Buzz. Edited by Barnabas Oretan (The Tech Buzz).· AI-generated image [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com) just threw down the gauntlet in the AI agent wars. The company announced Claude Duet today, a new autonomous agent designed for professionals and small business owners that directly challenges [Meta's](https://www.meta.com) Muse and [OpenAI's](https://www.openai.com) Dots. Built on the company's Claude Opus 5.5 model, Duet launches as a research preview across iOS, Android, and web platforms, marking Anthropic's most aggressive push yet into the rapidly heating AI agent market where tech giants are racing to automate knowledge work. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com) is making its move in the AI agent gold rush. The San Francisco-based startup announced Claude Duet today, positioning the new autonomous agent as a productivity powerhouse for professionals who need AI that doesn't just chat but actually gets work done. The timing isn't coincidental. With [Meta](https://www.meta.com) pushing Muse and [OpenAI](https://www.openai.com) betting big on Dots, the battle for who controls your digital workflow just went into overdrive. Claude Duet runs on Opus 5.5, Anthropic's latest model, and [according to the company's announcement](https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-duet), it's designed to function as a genuine work partner rather than a glorified search engine. Each morning, Duet sends users a curated brief highlighting the most important items across their connected apps. Throughout the day, it monitors those same apps and only surfaces notifications when something genuinely requires human attention. You can also hand off entire tasks and let it work autonomously. The research preview label is significant. It signals Anthropic is testing the waters while competitors race ahead, but it also buys the company time to refine the experience before a full-scale launch. The agent is available starting today as a standalone app on iOS and Android, plus through the existing Claude web interface. That multi-platform approach mirrors how [Anthropic has navigated recent cloud partnerships that turned contentious](https://www.techbuzz.ai/articles/anthropic-s-cloud-partners-turn-rivals-ahead-of-ipo) as the company's IPO speculation intensifies. Advertisement What sets Duet apart, at least on paper, is its focus on professionals and small business owners rather than enterprise teams or casual consumers. That's a different wedge than Meta's consumer-first Muse or OpenAI's developer-oriented Dots. AI Product.titleZh: AI Research Startup Flapping Airplanes Valued at $6 Billion in Round - Bloomberg
AI Product.content: # AI Research Startup Flapping Airplanes Valued at $6 Billion Flapping Airplanes, a year-old artificial intelligence startup, has raised $1 billion in funding at a $6 billion valuation — the latest example of investors betting on a newer crop of AI research labs that have yet to introduce commercial products. The financing, set to be announced Wednesday, was led by Index Ventures and Lux Capital. Other participants included Sequoia Capital, Alphabet Inc.’s GV and Kleiner Perkins. The company’s valuation, which includes the money raised, has quadrupled from a prior round in January. Founded in late 2025, Flapping Airplanes is one of a growing number of so-called AI neolabs, or startups that are initially focused on research rather than racing to launch artificial intelligence products and bolster revenue. Venture capital firms have poured billions of dollars into companies working on AI-driven scientific breakthroughs, self-improving AI systems and more. Flapping Airplanes is working on methods to train AI models on less data and less compute, as well as making the chips used to develop and run models more efficient, co-founder Asher Spector said in an interview. The effort to do more with less coincides with heightened scrutiny on the massive amount of capital companies are spending on chips and data centers to support AI development. “The basic thesis is demand for AI is going to outpace chip and data supply,” Spector said. “The company that’s going to be most successful, and create the most value for the world, is the one that can squeeze the most out of the inputs.” Given how much money is being spent on infrastructure for the current AI boom, wringing 10% more performance out of each chip would be “tremendously economically valuable,” he said.

Open Source AI.content: [English](/en/)[IT](/en/en-it/) # Krafton launches cost-efficient Raon-1 mini LLM to boost AI use in Korea 입력 2026.10.21. 17:08 [조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=biz.chosun.com) ![/Courtesy of Krafton](https://biz.chosun.com/resizer/v2/DTGOXSBDLFHZ5AJX3VIRZIB72M.jpg?auth=94fdbea9fe968b66a864fe6574a33f556c7de74a25a3a0b46a39fedb9b2ba5d5&width=616) /Courtesy of Krafton Krafton said on the 21st that it released a preview version of its self-developed high-efficiency large language model (LLM), "Raon-1 mini." Raon-1 mini is a 30 billion (30B) parameter LLM that Krafton independently handled end to end, from model design to training. It supports Korean and English and focuses on achieving both high performance and low operating expense. To that end, Krafton combined a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture with its self-developed linear attention technology. By activating only 4 billion (4B) of the total 30 billion parameters needed for a task, it reduced computation to speed up responses and lower inference expense. According to the company, Raon-1 mini showed superior performance compared with overseas models in its class, and on some evaluation metrics reached levels close to large domestic models. In particular, it showed strengths in natural Korean conversation, fast response speed, and accurately following user instructions. The ability to follow complex instructions, such as format specification or persona settings, is key to implementing AI agents that autonomously carry out multi-step tasks. Krafton views not only AI model performance but also expense efficiency in real service environments as a core competitive edge. As AI use expands across industries, the company judges it crucial to maintain high performance while lowering operating expense. The preview version has been released on the global AI open-source platform Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license. Anyone can download it for free and use it not only for research but also for commercial services and product development. Krafton plans to release an official version with improved performance and publish a technical report covering the model's training process and final performance. Lee Kang-uk, Krafton chief AI officer (CAIO), said, "The release of Raon-1 mini is the result of independently developing a competitive language model through Krafton's more than five years of accumulated AI research and development capabilities," and added, "As a cost-effective LLM that raises performance and lowers expense burden, we will broaden the use of AI across various industrial fields." ※ This article has been translated by AI. Open Source AI.content: [Skip to Main Navigation](#main) [![World Bank Blogs Logo](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/wbcollab/logo-en?qlt=90&fmt=webp&resMode=sharp2 "World Bank Blogs Logo")](/en/home) Published on [Data Blog](/en/opendata) # Beyond chat demos: evaluating LLM systems at scale with DeepEval * [Rafael Sevilla Macalaba](/en/team/r/rafael-sevilla-macalaba) * [Aivin Solatorio](/en/team/a/aivin-solatorio) This page in: * [English](/en/opendata/beyond-chat-demos--evaluating-llm-systems-at-scale-with-deepeval) * [English](/en/opendata/beyond-chat-demos--evaluating-llm-systems-at-scale-with-deepeval) ![Beyond chat demos: evaluating LLM systems at scale with DeepEval](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/wbcollab/generative-ai-1?qlt=90&fmt=webp&resMode=sharp2 "Beyond chat demos: evaluating LLM systems at scale with DeepEval") The evaluation framework combines persona composition, live multi-turn simulation, metric pre-filtering, and LLM-based scoring to test chatbot reliability at scale. / Image: Shutterstock Building a generative AI chat prototype has become straightforward. With a large language model (LLM), a vector database, a frontend interface, and an AI coding assistant, a developer can assemble a working demo in days. However, deploying such applications at institutions like the World Bank Group—where data accuracy, policy context, and citation verifiability are essential—requires far more than a working proof of concept. How do you guarantee an LLM assistant remains reliable across hundreds of user requests? How do you ensure it does not hallucinate indicators, skip citations, or lose context over multi-turn dialogues? How do you measure response quality for questions users have not yet asked? To address these challenges, we built an automated, persona-driven evaluation framework using Confident AI's open-source [DeepEval](https://deepeval.com/) library as our scoring backbone. While DeepEval provides core metric primitives, our framework introduces custom innovations: dynamic persona composition, intelligent pre-filtering, and a replay mechanism for rapid rubric iteration. Originally created for the Data360 Chat Assistant, this framework is now packaged as a reusable blueprint for building trustworthy AI applications across the institution ([GitHub Repository](https://github.com/worldbank/data-ai-chatbot)). ### The unpredictable path of multi-turn chat Traditional software testing is linear: input A yields output B. For conversational AI, this approach fails because user interactions are dynamic, branching dialogues. A user might greet the assistant, ask for GDP trends, request data formatted in a table, compare neighboring countries, and finally request a chart. ![Image](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/wbcollab/Screenshot-2026-10-21-152106?qlt=90&fmt=webp&resMode=sharp2) Conversation Turn Progression Evaluating isolated responses misses compounding multi-turn failures: * **Context Drift:** The model forgets constraints (such as country or year range) specified in earlier turns. * **Orchestration Failures:** The router correctly classifies intent on Turn 1 but strays onto an incorrect path on Turn 3. * **State and Transport Breaks:** Persistent Server-Sent Events (SSE) data streams can cut off mid-transit, or database session state can fail to reload, forcing the model to restart. To catch these failures, our framework executes tests directly against the live chatbot API—requesting guest auth tokens, persisting PostgreSQL session IDs, and parsing streamed responses to simulate real user sessions. ![Image](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/wbcollab/Screenshot-2026-10-21-152125?qlt=90&fmt=webp&resMode=sharp2) Chatbot Evaluation System Dataflow ### From isolation to standardization Across large organizations, teams build specialized GenAI applications to query databases, summarize documents, or scan research. On Tuesday, the Chinese AI lab [published DeepInfer](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer), the inference framework behind its large-scale production services, as open-source code under the Apache 2.0 license, with Huawei’s Ascend 950 chips supported alongside Nvidia’s newest GPUs. ![DeepSeek V4 - artistic interpretation. Image credit: Alius Noreika / AI](https://www.technology.org/texorgwp/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/deepseek-ai-software-model-v4-photo.jpg) ![DeepSeek V4 - artistic interpretation. Image credit: Alius Noreika / AI](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%201365%201006%22%3E%3C/svg%3E) ### **Key Takeaways** ## What Comes in the Box DeepInfer bundles optimized kernels from DeepSeek’s earlier open projects, including FlashMLA, DeepGEMM and DeepEP, plus TileKernels, DeepSelect and custom TileLang kernels. It spreads work across chips with attention data parallelism, balanced context parallelism, and expert parallelism for mixture-of-experts layers with load balancing (EPLB). A decoding method called DSpark drafts tokens ahead and uses confidence estimates to decide when to verify them. By default it drafts up to five tokens. Other features include bounded replay for sliding-window attention, which trims prefill work, and an asynchronous scheduler that overlaps CPU batch planning with chip execution. Developers can also force outputs into a regex, JSON schema or EBNF grammar. Two features, batch-invariant inference and deterministic sampling, work on Nvidia hardware only. They keep results identical across runs with the same inputs. DeepSeek also published deepseek-recipe, a component that turns text into tokens and back the same way its official API does. Open Source AI.titleZh: LiteLLM supply chain attack hoovers up passwords and secrets
Open Source AI.content: security # LiteLLM supply chain attack hoovers up passwords and secrets Plus a RAT for good measure - get threat hunting now ### READ MORE * #### Auto tech startup claims it traced hack attempt back to rival's IP address * #### Palo Alto's firewall OS has been under attack from multiple ransomware groups since June * #### 'Password1' and a forgotten test account land Welsh outfits in hot water * #### Broadcom Wi-Fi bug turns sweet 16, still lets strangers hijack your router * #### ConnectWise turns off its SaaS-y backup, security, and management services to probe security SNAFU Unknown crims compromised LiteLLM's release process on Wednesday, distributing a malicious version (1.107.0) containing malware designed to steal cloud and AI credentials and a remote access trojan (RAT) capable of executing arbitrary code on infected machines through PyPI and Docker registries. PyPI quarantined the trojanized version of the popular open source AI gateway within hours, and the Docker image (litellm/litellm:1.107.0) was removed from both Docker Hub and GHCR soon after - but anyone who ran the compromised package on any platform should assume their secrets have been stolen. “Check for /tmp/.pc\_once\_\* (the exfil has already fired if this file exists) and /tmp/remote\_code\_loader.lock (the C2 daemon ran or is still running if this file exists),” advised Aikido Security malware hunter Ilyas Makari. “The same applies to anyone who ran the official Docker image litellm/litellm:1.107.0, or pulled it via the latest, main-latest, or main-stable tags.” The most recent safe version is v1.106.2. While it’s too early to tell the scale of this latest LiteLLM supply chain attack – an earlier LiteLLM compromise in March potentially exposed more than 2,500 organizations and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines worldwide, according to CloudSEK – make sure to take these measures seriously, and check environments for any indicators of compromise. Aikido, Google’s Wiz cloud security biz, and supply-chain security provider Socket have all published extensive threat-hunting and mitigation instructions for LiteLLM users and security teams, so give those a read stat. LiteLLM, developed by BerriAI, provides a common interface for LLM providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini, and receives about 23 million weekly downloads. This means a compromised installation can run alongside LLM provider API keys, cloud identities, and database connection strings - and expose a ton of valuable credentials, secrets, and other sensitive data to whoever uploaded the malicious package. “Teams using 1.107.0 should stop deploying it and investigate environments where Python ran after installation, including proxy containers and CI runners,” Socket researchers said on Wednesday. The malicious version was uploaded at 11:39 UTC, and according to Wiz kids Benjamin Read and Rami McCarthy, the payload originates with malicious commits made on github.com/Berri-AI/litellm, which is a hyphenated variant of the legitimate BerriAI organization. Miscreants used this repo to inject the three malicious files into the LiteLLM release pipeline. These, according to Makari, include cook.pth, which causes the second file, cook.py, to run automatically every time Python is invoked on the machine, without any additional user action. Meanwhile, cook.py contains the infostealer, and the third file, sitecustomize.py, is the RAT. Python also executes the RAT at interpreter startup, and this file spawns a background daemon that polls the attacker's infrastructure every hour for new commands to execute. Upon executing, the infostealer harvests a ton of sensitive data across 16 modules targeting browsers, cloud providers, and AI services, according to Read and McCarthy. It steals browser credentials and cookies from Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari, along with AWS credentials from ~/.aws/, environment variables, and EC2/ECS instance metadata (IMDS). October 21, 2026 by [Stuart Pitts](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/stuartpitts/ "Posts by Stuart Pitts") [0 Comments](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/cloud-partners-europe-sovereign-safety-open-agents/#disqus_thread) Share This Article * [X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents https%3A%2F%2Fblogs.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fcloud-partners-europe-sovereign-safety-open-agents%2F) * [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fblogs.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fcloud-partners-europe-sovereign-safety-open-agents%2F) * [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fblogs.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fcloud-partners-europe-sovereign-safety-open-agents%2F&title=NVIDIA+Cloud+Partners+Scale+Across+Europe+%E2%80%94+Sovereign%2C+Open+and+Built+for+Safe+AI+Agents+%7C+NVIDIA+Blog) * [Copy link Link copied!](# "Copy link to clipboard") ![](https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ai-cloud-announcement-gtc-berlin-social-1920x1080-5852877-r2-1280x720.png) Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design.  [NVIDIA Cloud Partners](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/gpu-cloud-computing/partners/) across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. [Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements](https://blogs.nvidia.com/gtc-berlin-2026-news/) ## **Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure** Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the [NVIDIA DSX Platform](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/products/dsx/maxlps/) to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. The A5X instances combine NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs with ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and Google's fourth-generation liquid-cooling technology, creating an integrated platform for AI training, inference, and large-scale reinforcement learning. The rollout starts in the U.S. before expanding to Europe, as hyperscalers race to offer the most powerful AI infrastructure to enterprise customers. [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com) is making its biggest bet yet on AI infrastructure, announcing that [NVIDIA's](https://www.nvidia.com) Vera Rubin-powered A5X instances will reach general availability next month. The move puts Google squarely in competition with rivals racing to offer the most powerful cloud-based AI training platforms. The A5X instances represent a full-stack approach to AI infrastructure. They bring together NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs, the company's ConnectX-9 SuperNICs for high-speed networking, Google Cloud's proprietary Virgo Network, and Google's fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology. It's an integrated system designed for the most demanding AI workloads, from training massive models to running inference at scale and handling complex reinforcement learning tasks. The timing couldn't be more strategic. Just hours after [NVIDIA unveiled its full local AI stack at GTC Berlin](https://www.techbuzz.ai/articles/nvidia-unleashes-full-local-ai-stack-at-gtc-berlin), including RTX Spark and DGX systems for on-device intelligence, the company is now extending its reach into cloud infrastructure. The dual approach shows NVIDIA hedging its bets across both edge and cloud computing as enterprises figure out where their AI workloads will ultimately run. Google's deployment strategy starts domestic before going global. The initial U.S. rollout next month will be followed by European expansion, though specific timing and regions remain under wraps. The phased approach suggests Google is being cautious about scaling what's essentially a complex, power-hungry infrastructure play that requires significant data center modifications. Advertisement The liquid-cooling component is particularly telling. Google's fourth-generation cooling technology isn't just about keeping chips from overheating - it's about density. Modern AI accelerators generate so much heat that traditional air cooling can't pack them close enough together for optimal performance. Will the network carry someone else’s value, or will it become the platform on which that value is created? Inference gives service providers a strong opportunity to choose the second path. They already have assets that the AI economy needs: distributed facilities, power, trusted infrastructure, and reach in the regions where enterprises and governments operate. Those assets become more valuable when they can operate as one system. An inference request may have suitable capacity near by, yet still travel farther than necessary because the network does not have enough context about the workload. The best destination may depend on latency, available throughput, cost, or a jurisdictional requirement. Conventional reachability alone does not express all those needs. At [NVIDIA GTC](https://www.nvidia.com/gtc/) Berlin, Cisco is [introducing a blueprint for AI Inference Routing,](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/solutions/collateral/design-zone/ai-inference-wan-wp.html) one of several areas where Cisco and NVIDIA are working together for service providers. It outlines how service providers can place, route, secure, and assure inference across a distributed footprint, from a single edge site to a sovereign regional hub. The goal is to solve utilization through placement and routing rather than more infrastructure. Capacity sitting idle in one region can be applied to demand in another, and the resulting service can be built on demand rather than pre-provisioned site by site. ## **Why inference changes the role of the network** An AI prompt may look like a simple exchange between a user and a model, but the underlying transaction crosses a distributed system. It can [pass through the Internet or an enterprise network, policy engines, API gateways, model-routing layers, CPU serving infrastructure, and a GPU fabric before the response returns](https://blogs.cisco.com/sp/why-ai-inference-is-becoming-a-networking-issue). That makes placement and connectivity part of the application experience. This matters even more as inference spreads across central AI factories, regional data centers, metro locations, and edge sites. One request may need the lowest-delay path. Another may need to remain within a national boundary. A third may prioritize cost while still meeting a performance objective. Service providers need a way to translate those requirements into network behavior, and to verify with measurement that the service is delivering what was committed...
